# Pinned supplementary package notices

These exact upstream files supplement archive-missing license text for the verified Foundation API/worker NuGet closure. They do not replace the original nuspec license expression, repository identity, copyright or archive contents. `bundle.json` binds each package ID/version to its actual signed-archive SHA-512, original nuspec SHA-256, repository URL and exact commit. Source files retain their original bytes, SHA-256, Git blob SHA-1 and commit-addressed source URL.

The 24 October 2026 acquisition used the GitHub connector's commit-addressed contents metadata and anonymous HTTPS reads of those exact official raw URLs. Downloaded bytes matched the connector's Git blob hashes before being retained. No latest branch, version-adjacent package or generic replacement text was used. Treat retained HTML notice files as text; no upstream script/instruction is executed.

Twenty-two package bindings have exact declared commits and verified supplementary texts. This includes thirteen of the original fourteen archive-notice-absence findings and nine Microsoft.Extensions packages whose archives contain third-party notices but no own declared MIT license file. The extra nine use the same independently verified dotnet/dotnet commit, not a version-adjacent license. `SQLitePCLRaw.bundle_e_sqlite3/3.0.5` declares no repository commit in its verified nuspec; its missing text remains unresolved. Do not borrow another SQLite package's commit or infer a version binding. The exact MCP 2.2.0 LICENSE describes a licensing transition and retains MIT/Apache/documentation context; both MCP package bindings therefore keep `UpstreamLicenseTransitionReviewRequired` in addition to their unmodified Apache-2.0 nuspec declaration.

Run `scripts/Test-FoundationPackageNoticePins.ps1` for offline source-manifest hash/provenance checks. It reports `actualPackageBindingsVerified=false`; it does not read actual NuGet packages. Optional `-Refetch` reads only the already-reviewed, exact commit URLs into a new artifact directory and compares their original bytes, with a 30-second deadline covering headers and body plus a 512 KiB cap. It never updates this source, restores packages, executes package code or signs in. `New-FoundationDependencyEvidence.ps1` additionally checks every used supplement against the actual verified package metadata and emits it in the existing dependency report/notices output.

All seven first-party project licenses remain `NOASSERTION`; proprietary binary and source-distribution terms are separate draft work. No license grant, ownership representation, legal clearance, signing, source freeze or production qualification is created here. Full upstream repository notices are retained as context; their applicability to every packaged/embedded byte still needs review.
